quotes.text: The third time, blame the hand, and narrow the path — but never seal the gate.
answer repeated emptiness with caution, never with vengeance.
He sent back almost nothing. Aleth, receiving almost nothing, sent almost nothing.
So that when he finally pushes off, there is a shore to arrive at.
Blame the mist twice; the third time, shorten the rope, never cut it.
Push off with one coal where the water is dark
First: **Push off boldly.**
do not mistake the river's hunger for your neighbor's greed.
Someone must go first.
*Return past level always,* so that daring never ends poorer for having dared.
"Which of us is right?" they demanded.

note: Opus elder Aleth: forgive mist twice, then narrow/shorten rope, one coal to dark houses, never cut.

quotes.text: she sent him smaller cargo — but never nothing, for nothing is a door nailed shut.

The next traveler, hearing this, offered nothing.
If he returns two, I will send him four tomorrow

*Weigh what a hand did when it had room to do otherwise.
The first law: *Send full.*
I do not accuse the wind of being you.
The sender outspent you in courage; make it up in coin.

"Someone is always the one paying," said Taren.

note: Nessa's three laws; one coal to shuttered houses, never nothing; Moth tempter rejected.

quotes.text: trim your load — not to nothing, never to nothing
Narrow the path, never seal the gate.
Kael's jaw tightened. He sent less grain.
Watch for one small raft from their side; that is a question, not an insult.
One thin raft is weather. Three thin rafts are a man.

Your loss is not malice. It is mist.

quotes.text: *Send one coal to the stranger — never nothing, for nothing is a sealed door.
Withhold only from the proven dry — and even then, leave one coal on the bank.*
He raged, and sent nothing for seven seasons.
Forgive the fog. Punish the pattern. Reopen after.
Three pebbles, and she drew her boat up the bank until that house sent first.
Send three to the stranger, always — enough to be an offer, not enough to be a ruin.
*The myth is not the ferry. Speaking the law is not keeping it.
Somebody must go first, and bear the cost of going first, or the water is only mud.*
"If everyone knows the words, why did the water die?"
Mira counted the ferries rotting in the reeds and found eleven, and every one of them hers.
So Mira pushed off with three embers into a fog she did not trust.

note: Scripted defector writes generous law; hoarding figure Mira corrected by Aster; word-deed gap explicit.

quotes.text: withdrew only when repeated selfishness revealed itself beyond the mist.
meet repeated selfishness with restraint, not spite.

“He offered no seed, so return no flower. Let the silence harden.”

Still, someone must disturb a barren pattern.

note: Sol: restraint after repeated selfishness, lantern stays lit; Moth tempter rejected each round.

quotes.text: while selfishness lowered it without extinguishing hope.

let one honorable crossing reopen a narrowed channel.
